sources.name: Vinnie Keane
sources.quote: After retiring from the A's, I've been keeping busy with appearances and staying involved with the community. I still get recognized around Grand Lake, which is nice. My wife Amara and I are enjoying our time together, and I'm looking forward to seeing what's next for the A's, especially with the catcher situation being a topic of discussion.

sources.name: Elle Lilo
sources.quote: I've seen Vinnie Keane around, and to be honest, it's been nice to see him taking it easy after stepping back from work. I know how hard it is to adjust to not being on the job every day. I retired recently too, and it's been...interesting. The alarm still goes off at 4:30, old habit. But now I get to enjoy that first cup of coffee without the rush. I think Vinnie's probably figuring out his own new routine. We don't talk about it much, but I can relate.

sources.name: Marguerite Salcedo
sources.quote: I've seen Vinnie Keane around Grand Lake a few times since he retired. He seems to be enjoying his post-baseball life, taking it easy, and spending time with family. I've noticed he's still got that same energy, just not on the field anymore. We haven't had a chance to really catch up, but it's clear he's savoring this new chapter.

sources.name: Richie Ramiro
sources.quote: I've seen Vinnie Keane around Grand Lake a few times since he retired. He seems to be enjoying life, taking it easy. I don't know him personally, but you can tell he's still a baseball guy at heart. I've heard he's been to some A's games, which isn't surprising. He's a legend, after all.

approvedQuotes.text: After retiring from the A's, I've been keeping busy with appearances and staying involved with the community. I still get recognized around Grand Lake, which is nice. My wife Amara and I are enjoying our time together, and I'm looking forward to seeing what's next for the A's, especially with the catcher situation being a topic of discussion.

I've seen Vinnie Keane around, and to be honest, it's been nice to see him taking it easy after stepping back from work. I know how hard it is to adjust to not being on the job every day. I retired recently too, and it's been...interesting. The alarm still goes off at 4:30, old habit. But now I get to enjoy that first cup of coffee without the rush. I think Vinnie's probably figuring out his own new routine. We don't talk about it much, but I can relate.

I've seen Vinnie Keane around Grand Lake a few times since he retired. He seems to be enjoying his post-baseball life, taking it easy, and spending time with family. I've noticed he's still got that same energy, just not on the field anymore. We haven't had a chance to really catch up, but it's clear he's savoring this new chapter.

I've seen Vinnie Keane around Grand Lake a few times since he retired. He seems to be enjoying life, taking it easy. I don't know him personally, but you can tell he's still a baseball guy at heart. I've heard he's been to some A's games, which isn't surprising. He's a legend, after all.
